The '''2020–21 season''' was [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City Football Club]]'s [[List of Manchester City F.C. seasons|119th in existence]] and their 19th consecutive season in the [[English football league system|top flight]] of [[Football in England|English football]]. In addition to the [[2020–21 Premier League|domestic league]], Manchester City participated in this season's editions of the [[2020–21 FA Cup|FA Cup]] and the [[2020–21 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]], as well as the [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]], entering the competition for the tenth consecutive year, with their best result being a semi-final in [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League|2016]]. The season covered the period from 16 August 2020 to 30 June 2021.

During this season, City achieved a remarkable [[winning streak]], which ran 82 days from December 2020 to March 2021. During this run, City broke the records for most consecutive wins by a top flight English team in all competitions (21), the most consecutive league wins by a top flight team from the start of a calendar year (13) and equalled their club record for 28 games unbeaten in all competitions.<ref>{{Cite magazine|agency=Associated Press|title=Man City Wins Record 15th Straight to Reach FA Cup Quarters|url=https://www.si.com/soccer/2021/02/10/manchester-city-swansea-fa-cup-video-record-winning-streak|access-date=18 February 2021|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=10 February 2021 |language=en-us}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Pollard|first=Rob|title=City set another English top-flight record|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/man-city-english-top-flight-record-10-win-start-of-year-63749183|access-date=19 February 2021|website=www.mancity.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Edgar|first=Bill|title=The numbers behind Manchester City's 28-game unbeaten run|newspaper=[[The Times]]|language=en|url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/article/the-numbers-behind-manchester-citys-28-game-unbeaten-run-vk82gh0cr|access-date=7 March 2021|issn=0140-0460}}</ref> City also set a record run of consecutive away wins in all competitions for a top flight team (20), a club and English record run of consecutive unbeaten away matches (23) and an English record run of consecutive away league wins (12) during this season.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Leigh|first=Neil|title=Record-breaking City too strong for Gladbach|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/gladbach-city-champions-league-last-16-first-leg-report-63749789|access-date=24 February 2021|website=www.mancity.com|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|last=Leigh|first=Neil|title=City set new Club record with win over Toffees|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/city-set-new-record-with-17th-unbeaten-away-game-63751865|access-date=20 March 2021|website=www.mancity.com|language=en}}</ref>

On 14 April, City advanced to the Champions League semi-finals for the first time [[2015–16 Manchester City F.C. season|in five years]], after three consecutive quarter-final eliminations in 2018–20.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56754630|title=Man City want to build more history after reaching Champions League semi-final, says Guardiola|website=BBC Sport|date=15 April 2021|access-date=4 May 2021}}</ref> On 25 April, the Blues defeated [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham]] to win their record-equalling fourth consecutive, and eighth overall, League Cup title.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/56882358|title=Manchester City beat Tottenham in Carabao Cup: Phil Foden shows potential for greatness|website=BBC Sport|date=25 April 2021|access-date=4 May 2021}}</ref> On 4 May, City reached the Champions League final for the first time in their history as they defeated [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] 4–1 on aggregate in the semi-finals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/champions-league/2020-2021/manchester-city-v-paris-saint-germain-follow-live_sto8302793/story.shtml|title=Sublime Manchester City reach first Champions League final|website=Eurosport|date=4 May 2021|access-date=4 May 2021}}</ref> On 11 May, the Citizens were officially confirmed as Premier League champions for the third time in four seasons following a 1–2 home defeat of second-placed [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] at the hands of [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]]. On 29 May, City were defeated 1–0 by [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in the [[2021 UEFA Champions League Final|Champions League final]], ending their hopes of winning a treble and clinching the first European trophy since [[1969–70 Manchester City F.C. season|1970]].

[[Rúben Dias]], [[Phil Foden]], [[Kevin De Bruyne]] and [[Pep Guardiola]] were amongst the City representatives recognised in the various end of season awards.<ref name=":3">{{cite news|title=De Bruyne wins second PFA men's award|publisher=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57376601|date=6 June 2021|access-date=9 June 2021}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite news|title=Dias & Guardiola win Premier League awards|publisher=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57368530|date=6 June 2021|access-date=9 June 2021}}</ref> The season was the first since [[2009–10 Manchester City F.C. season|2009–10]] without [[David Silva]], who departed to join [[Real Sociedad]] and a first since [[2015-16 Manchester City F.C. season|2015-16]] without [[Leroy Sané]], who departed to join [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]].

==Season summary==
===Start of season===
The 2020–21 season began in September 2020 during the global [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. The protocols used to permit the [[2019–20 Premier League]] season to be concluded were extended into the new season so that professional sport could be played in front of a television audience, with the expectation that fans would be able to attend games in person once infection rates fell and public health restrictions could be lifted. However, by the end of March 2021 only one game involving Manchester City (away against [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] on 19 December) had been played in front of (2,000) spectators.

City had invested heavily in their central defence during the summer with the purchases of [[Rúben Dias]] from [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] and [[Nathan Aké]] from [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]]. [[Nicolás Otamendi]] moved in the opposite direction to Dias to join the Portuguese side. The transfers were designed to improve the team's perceived weakness in the defensive area since [[Vincent Kompany]] had left City at the end of the [[2018–19 Manchester City F.C. season|2018–19 season]]. [[Ferran Torres]] was also signed from [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] as a replacement winger for [[Leroy Sané]], who had departed for [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]].

Some initially inconsistent league results left City in the bottom half of the table when they were defeated 2–0 by [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] on 21 November (albeit with a game in hand over many of the clubs above them). However, their league form improved for the remainder of the year as the Blues ended 2020 with no further defeats. This was mainly due to City's defensive record, with them registering six consecutive clean sheets in all competitions and ending the year with 13 clean sheets in total from 23 games played. City were undefeated in cup competitions by the end of 2020, reaching the semi-finals of the [[2020–21 EFL Cup|Carabao Cup]] for the fourth consecutive year and, more importantly, the [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League knockout phase|knockout stage]] of the [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] for the eighth consecutive season, with their highest ever group stage points total (16 points).

Initially, City were less effective at the other end of the pitch than they had been in the previous three seasons. In part, this was due to the injury of [[Sergio Agüero]], that had been carried over from the end of the prior season, and further injuries to Agüero and [[Gabriel Jesus]] that left City without a recognised first team striker in the squad until the beginning of December.

===Christmas and New Year===
A [[SARS-CoV-2]] outbreak at the [[Etihad Campus|City Football Academy]] over Christmas led to the postponement of City's game versus [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] on 28 December to 17 February, and up to nine first team players were in isolation at the beginning of the new year, including, once again, Sergio Agüero and Gabriel Jesus.

Nevertheless, City's good form continued into January 2021, with the team ending the month with a perfect 100% win record in all nine of their competitive fixtures, the most by a team in the top four tiers of English football in a single month since the formation of the [[English Football League|Football League]] in [[1888–89 Football League|1888]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Nine In Nine: City's Perfect January Sets New English Football Records |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/perfect-january-record-nine-wins-63747766 |website=mancity.com |access-date=1 February 2021}}</ref> In the process they beat [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] in a single legged semi-final to reach City's fourth consecutive [[2021 EFL Cup Final|League Cup final]], reached the fifth round of the [[2020–21 FA Cup|FA Cup]], extended their unbeaten run in the Premier League to twelve games with eight consecutive wins, climbed the table from 9th to 1st and achieved nineteen games unbeaten with twelve consecutive wins in all competitions to the end of January.

At the halfway point of the season (Game Week 19), Manchester City were leading the Premier League with 41 points from 19 games, a point ahead of Manchester United and with a game in hand.

In February and March, City maintained their form to extend their winning run in all competitions to 21 games, a new record for a top flight side in English football. They also matched their previous club record of 28 games unbeaten and broke their own national top flight record by winning fourteen consecutive away games in all competitions.<ref name=":1" /> [[Pep Guardiola]] went on to record his 200th win when his side defeated [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham]] 2–1 at the [[City of Manchester Stadium]]. At the time, he had also achieved a higher win percentage managing Manchester City than he had when he managed [[F.C. Barcelona|Barcelona]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=11 February 2021|title=Guardiola's record at Man City is officially better than his time at Barca|url=https://global.espn.com/football/blog-the-toe-poke/story/4312764/guardiolas-record-at-man-city-is-officially-better-than-his-time-at-barca-as-his-list-of-records-grows|access-date=18 February 2021|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref>

On 7 February, City thrashed [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] 4–1 on the road to achieve their first victory at [[Anfield]] in almost 18 years and only their third win there in 50 games since 1956.<ref>{{cite web |title=Quiz: Name Liverpool and Man City starting XIs from 2003 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55892650 |website=bbcsport.co.uk |date=5 February 2021 |access-date=11 February 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/english-premier-league/story/4308060/man-city-thrash-liverpool-to-make-emphatic-statement-as-premier-league-champions-elect|title=Champions-elect Man City make emphatic statement at Liverpool|date=7 February 2021|website=ESPN.com}}</ref> Their winning run was ended when City were beaten 2–0 at the City of Manchester Stadium by [[Manchester derby|rivals]] Manchester United on 7 March.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56227458|title=Man Utd 'not thinking' about title|work=BBC Sport |date=5 March 2021 }}</ref> On 16 March, City defeated [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]] 2–0 (4–0 on aggregate) and advanced to the Champions League quarter-finals for the fourth year in a row.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/manchester-city-v-borussia-monchengladbach-ucl-round-of-16-match-report-63751520|title=Hungry City cruise into Champions League last eight|first=David|last=Clayton|website=www.mancity.com}}</ref> On 20 March, the Blues scored two late goals to beat [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] on the road and advance to the FA Cup semi-finals for the third consecutive year.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/everton-manchester-city-fa-cup-match-report-63751861|title=Gundogan and De Bruyne goals put City into FA Cup semi-final |date=3 April 2021 }}</ref>

On 29 March, the club announced that Sergio Agüero would be leaving at the end of the season on expiration of his contract. In 10 seasons at City Agüero had become, at the time, the club's [[List of Manchester City F.C. records and statistics#Goalscorers|all-time leading goalscorer]], the [[Premier League records and statistics#Goals|fourth highest goalscorer]] in the history of the Premier League, the goalscorer with the most Premier League goals at a single club (and its leading non-English scorer) and the holder of a plethora of club goal scoring records. At the time he was also City's [[List of Manchester City F.C. records and statistics#Players with the most titles won at the club|most decorated player of all time]] with fifteen league and cup winner medals. He would also be remembered in club and English football history as the winning goalscorer at the denouement of the [[2011–12 Premier League]] season, when City won their first title in 44 years by [[Manchester City F.C. 3–2 Queens Park Rangers F.C.|defeating Queens Park Rangers 3–2]], with Agüero scoring in the 94th minute to clinch the title for Manchester City. The Blues finished ahead of closest rivals Manchester United on goal difference.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Pollard|first=Rob|title=City to bid emotional farewell to Club legend Sergio Aguero this summer|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/sergio-aguero-to-leave-manchester-city-63752641|access-date=30 March 2021|website=www.mancity.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Season run-in===
In April it was announced that the Carabao Cup final between City and Tottenham Hotspur at [[Wembley Stadium|Wembley]] would be a test for the return of spectators to sports events with 8,000 tickets available: the two clubs would be allocated 2,000 tickets each with the remaining 4,000 made available for the residents of [[London Borough of Brent|Brent]] and local [[National Health Service|NHS]] workers. All attendees would have to consent to mandatory [[COVID-19 testing]] before and after the event, travel only by car or on specially chartered trains and coaches from [[Manchester]] and provide contact data for track and trace purposes. The match would be the first outdoor sports event with supporters of the teams involved in attendance in the UK in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Carabao Cup final: Manchester City and Tottenham receive 2,000 tickets each at Wembley with Covid testing requirements in place|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12274216/carabao-cup-final-manchester-city-and-tottenham-receive-2000-tickets-each-at-wembley-with-covid-testing-requirements-in-place|access-date=2021-04-13|website=Sky Sports|language=en}}</ref>

City began their April and May season run-in still in contention for an unprecedented [[List of association football teams to have won four or more trophies in one season#Four titles in one season|quadruple]] of major English and European titles, a feat they had been close to achieving in three of their previous seven seasons, and which they previously came closest to in the [[2018–19 Manchester City F.C. season|2018–19 season]] when the Blues won an also unprecedented [[Treble (association football)#Domestic trebles|domestic treble]]. On 1 April, they led the league on 74 points, 14 points ahead of Manchester United in second place who had a game in hand.<ref>{{Cite news|title=How Man City are battling history to land the quadruple|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56591844|access-date=2021-04-13}}</ref>

This lead narrowed to 11 points on Game Week 31 when City suffered a 1–2 home defeat to [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]], leaving them requiring at most 11 points from their remaining six fixtures to secure the league title. This defeat occurred between the two legs of City's Champions League quarter-finals against [[Borussia Dortmund]]. The first leg at home in Manchester ended as a 2–1 victory to City and Guardiola made seven changes to his team in the Leeds fixture to rest key players for the second leg in Dortmund.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Foden scores late as City beat Dortmund|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56641944|access-date=2021-04-13}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Ten-man Leeds beat leaders Man City|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56622155|access-date=2021-04-13}}</ref>

On 14 April, City defeated Borussia Dortmund 2–1 away from home (4–2 on aggregate) and advanced to the Champions League semi-finals for the first time under Pep Guardiola and only second time in their history.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Mahrez and Foden send Man City into last four|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56736853|access-date=2021-04-14}}</ref>

On 17 April, City's hopes for an unprecedented quadruple were tarnished, as the Blues were defeated 1–0 by Chelsea in the FA Cup semi-final at Wembley, the second consecutive time City had been eliminated at this stage.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2021/apr/17/chelsea-v-manchester-city-fa-cup-semi-final-live|title=Chelsea 1-0 Manchester City: FA Cup semi-final – as it happened|newspaper=The Guardian|date=17 April 2021|last1=Murray|first1=Scott}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/56725442|title=Chelsea end Man City's quadruple hopes|work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

The following day, 18 April, it was announced that City had joined the proposed [[European Super League]] as one of its twelve founder members together with the five other "[[Big Six (English football)|Big Six]]" English football clubs.<ref>{{cite news|title='Big six' agree to join 'Super League'|language=en-GB|publisher=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56795811|access-date=21 April 2021}}</ref> However, the announcement led to widespread condemnation from [[The Football Association]], the [[Premier League]], [[UEFA]] and [[FIFA]], as well as from the UK's [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative]] [[Government of the United Kingdom|government]] and [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]].<ref>{{cite news|title=European Super League Q&A - what happens next?|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56807310|access-date=21 April 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=It's not sport if success is guaranteed - Guardiola|language=en-GB|publisher=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/av/football/56819670|access-date=21 April 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Brennan|first=Stuart|date=20 April 2021|title=Guardiola opposed European Super League plan to increase congested fixture list|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/pep-guardiola-opposes-european-super-20428611|access-date=21 April 2021|website=Manchester Evening News}}</ref> Within 48 hours of the initial announcement on 20 April, City announced that they had withdrawn from the Super League to be followed shortly by the other five English clubs. By the following day, only three of the original founders – Barcelona, [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] and [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] – remained committed, and it seemed that the proposal had collapsed.<ref>{{Cite news|title=ESL cannot now proceed - Agnelli|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56830308|access-date=21 April 2021}}</ref>

===End of season=== 
On 25 April, City defeated Tottenham Hotspur 1–0 in the League Cup final to lift their first trophy of the season. This victory was the club's fourth consecutive EFL Cup title and their eighth overall, matching the records held by Liverpool.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Man City beat Spurs to lift Carabao Cup|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56790307|access-date=2021-04-25}}</ref> On 4 May, City reached their first ever European Cup / Champions League final by defeating [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint Germain]] 2–0 (4–1 on aggregate) in the semi-finals.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Man City reach first Champions League final|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56973031|access-date=2021-05-04}}</ref> They would face Chelsea in the [[2021 UEFA Champions League Final|final]], making it the third all-English final in the competition's history.

On 11 May, City were officially crowned Premier League champions, clinching their third title in four seasons and their fifth in ten seasons. The Blues previously failed to complete their league victory on the previous weekend, when they fielded a team with eight changes from the second leg of the Champions League semi-finals and were beaten 1–2 at home by Chelsea, but second-placed Manchester United's 1–2 home defeat to Leicester City three days later left City ten points ahead with only three games of the season left to play.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/56964843|accessdate=19 September 2021|title=Manchester City win Premier League title after Manchester United lose to Leicester|website=BBC|date=11 May 2021}}</ref> In the end, they won the league by twelve points from second-placed Manchester United. On 23 May, City completed the league season, beating Everton 5–0 in front of 10,000 spectators at the City of Manchester Stadium. This would be the club's only home game in front of fans that season. This was also Sergio Agüero's final home game in City colours, an occasion he marked by coming off the bench in the 65th minute and scoring two goals, mirroring his debut performance against [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea]] in August 2011 and also breaking [[Wayne Rooney]]'s record for most Premier League goals at a single club (184).

On 29 May, City were defeated 0–1 by Chelsea in the Champions League final in an anti-climactic performance. [[Kevin De Bruyne]] was brutally injured by [[Antonio Rüdiger]] in the second half, and [[N'Golo Kanté]]'s brilliant performance limited City's attacking options. Guardiola's decision not to start a [[Midfielder#Defensive midfielder|holding midfielder]] was also criticized as one of the reasons behind City's defeat.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/man-city-champions-league-final-b1856493.html|title=Man City vs Chelsea: Pep Guardiola explains no holding midfielder decision in Champions League final|website=independent.co.uk|publisher=[[The Independent]]|author=Mark Critchley|date=29 May 2021|access-date=29 May 2021}}</ref> Still, City's European breakthrough signified their most successful season to date and Pep Guardiola showed his pride in the runners-up medal.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0269-12650cedca55-37515f69768e-1000/|title=Man. City 0–1 Chelsea: Havertz gives Blues second Champions League triumph|website=UEFA|publisher=Union of European Football Associations|date=29 May 2021|access-date=29 May 2021}}</ref>

====Matches====
The league fixtures were announced on 20 August 2020.<ref>{{cite news|title=Premier League 2020/21 fixtures released|url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/1754980|access-date=20 August 2020|publisher=Premier League|date=20 August 2020}}</ref> The 2020–21 season officially began on 12 September 2020.<ref>{{cite news|title=Start date of 2020/21 season confirmed|url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/1603070|publisher=Premier League|access-date=9 September 2020}}</ref> However, clubs who had participated in the latter rearranged knockout rounds of the previous season's [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] and [[2019–20 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] competitions in August 2020 were allowed a further week to rest and prepare their squads for the new season. City's match at home against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], originally scheduled for gameweek 1, was therefore postponed until later in the season, and City instead started their campaign on the following Monday night away to [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]]. The Aston Villa home fixture was eventually rearranged for 20 January 2021.<ref>{{cite news|title=Confirmed Date and Time for Rearranged Villa Game|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/aston-villa-new-date-kick-off-time-63745017|publisher=Manchester City F.C.|access-date=31 December 2020}}</ref>

On 28 December 2020, City's away game at [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] was postponed four hours before kick off following a Premier League Board meeting. Manchester City lodged a request with the Premier League to rearrange the fixture following an increase in positive [[SARS-CoV-2]] test results received by the club earlier the same day, on top of four positive cases reported on Christmas Day for two non-playing staff, [[Kyle Walker]] and [[Gabriel Jesus]]. The Board agreed to rearrange the game as a safety precaution.<ref>{{cite news|title=Everton v Man City match postponed|url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/1957344|publisher=Premier League|access-date=29 December 2020}}</ref> The match was subsequently rescheduled for 17 February 2021.<ref>{{cite news|title=Everton v City: New Date for Toffees Clash|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/everton-v-city-fixture-update-63748042|publisher=Manchester City F.C.|access-date=5 February 2021}}</ref>

'''Note''': Match numbers indicated on the left hand side are references to the Game Weeks (GW) scheduled by the Premier League, and not the order in which matches were played after postponements and schedule alterations.<ref>{{cite web|title=Premier League Fixtures Season 2020/21|url=https://www.premierleague.com/fixtures|access-date=3 March 2021|publisher=Premier League}}</ref>

===FA Cup===
{{main|2020–21 FA Cup}}
The draw for the third round was held on 30 November 2020 by [[Robbie Savage]] and shown live on [[BBC One]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Premier League and Championship Clubs Joined The Emirates FA Cup in Third Round Draw|url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2020/nov/30/emirates-fa-cup-third-round-proper-draw-301120|publisher=The Football Association|access-date=30 November 2020}}</ref> The draws for the fourth and fifth round were both made on 11 January, conducted by [[Peter Crouch]].<ref>{{cite news|title=The Emirates FA Cup fourth and fifth round draw made|url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2021/jan/11/emirates-fa-cup-fourth-and-fifth-round-draws-20211101|publisher=The Football Association|access-date=11 January 2021}}</ref> The draw for the quarter-finals was held on 11 February 2021 and conducted by [[Karen Carney]].<ref>{{cite news|title=FA Cup draw: Everton host Man City, Leicester face Man Utd in quarter-finals|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56034228|access-date=11 February 2021}}</ref> The draw for the semi-finals was made, live on [[BBC One]], by [[Dion Dublin]] on 21 March 2021.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2021/mar/21/emirates-fa-cup-semi-final-draw-20210321|title=See the line-up for this season's Emirates FA Cup semi-finals after Sunday's draw|publisher=The Football Association|date=21 March 2021|access-date=21 March 2021}}</ref>

{{Football box collapsible
|date = 10 January 2021
|time = 13:30 [[Greenwich Mean Time|GMT]] ([[UTC±00:00|UTC±0]])
|round = [[2020–21 FA Cup#Third round proper|Third round]]

|note = The final was originally scheduled to be played at the [[Atatürk Olympic Stadium]] in [[Istanbul]]. However, on 12 May, UEFA announced it had been moved to Portugal since the high level of COVID-19 infection rates in Turkey had led the UK government to place travel to Turkey on its red list, meaning fans would have had to quarantine for ten days in a hotel at their expense after their return. Portugal at the same time was on the green list, which meant no travel restrictions at either end for those attending the final.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57071221|title=Champions League final moved to Porto and 12,000 Chelsea and Manchester City fans can attend|website=BBC Sport|date=13 May 2021|access-date=13 May 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/0269-1243f864391e-53c7874f0ae0-1000/|title=UEFA Champions League final to move to Portugal to allow 6,000 fans of each team to attend|website=UEFA|publisher=Union of European Football Associations|date=13 May 2021|access-date=13 May 2021}}</ref>
}}

==Awards==
In the end of season awards, [[Ederson (footballer, born 1993)|Ederson]] won the [[Premier League Golden Glove]] for the second consecutive season with his record of 19 [[Shutout#Association football|clean sheets]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Premier League Golden Glove award winners|url=http://www.premierleague.com/news/1206130|access-date=2021-06-09|website=www.premierleague.com|language=en}}</ref> Rúben Dias was recognised for his impressive debut season and the impact he had on leading the team's defence in winning the club's own [[List of Manchester City F.C. records and statistics#Player of the Year|Player of the Year]], the prestigious [[FWA Footballer of the Year|Football Writers Association Footballer of the Year]] and the [[Premier League Player of the Season]] awards.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Leigh|first=Neil|title=Dias wins 2021 Football Writers' Player of the Year award|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/ruben-dias-named-fwa-player-of-the-year-63757095|access-date=2021-06-09|website=www.mancity.com|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":4" /> [[Kevin De Bruyne]] won the [[PFA Players' Player of the Year]] for the second consecutive time.<ref name=":3" /> [[Phil Foden]] won the [[Premier League Young Player of the Season]] and [[PFA Young Player of the Year]], being recognised for his emergence as an outstanding English talent; and six City players were part of the [[PFA Team of the Year (2020s)|PFA Team of the Year]].<ref name="Leigh">{{Cite web|last=Leigh|first=Neil|title=Phil Foden named Premier League Young Player of the Year|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/phil-foden-named-premier-league-young-player-of-the-year-63758492|access-date=2021-06-09|website=www.mancity.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Edwards|first=John|title=City players dominate PFA Team of the Year|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/pfa-team-of-the-year-202021-63758414|access-date=2021-06-09|website=www.mancity.com|language=en}}</ref> Meanwhile, [[Pep Guardiola]] was awarded the [[League Managers Association Awards|League Managers Association Manager of the Year]] and the [[Premier League Manager of the Season]] awards.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Pollard|first=Rob|title=Guardiola wins LMA Manager of the Year award|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/pep-guardiola-named-lma-manager-of-the-year-63757478|access-date=2021-06-09|website=www.mancity.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Dias & Guardiola win Premier League awards|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57368530|access-date=2021-06-09}}</ref> Overall, this was the most awards won by City players and managers in the same season.
